rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN THE ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING ACT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 3, 3(a), 3(b), 3(g), 3(i), 7, 7(5), 7(6), 7(7), 7(11), 9(a), 9(c), 10, 11, 14(c), 15, and 16; AND REPEALING SECTION 20 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING ACT OF 2001”, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Aims to amend Republic Act No. 9160, also known as the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2001 (AMLA) to make it more effective in combating money laundering.
 
Seeks to amend AMLA by a) including casinos, real estate brokers, art dealers, and motor vehicle dealers as covered persons; b) changing the nomenclature for the covered person “jewelry dealers” in precious metals and stones to “dealers” in precious metals and stones and including jewelry dealers as a separate covered person; c) clarifying the definition of covered transactions depending on the covered person; d) designating the BSP as the Supervising Authority of foreign exchange dealers, money changers, and remittance and money and money transfer businesses, for purposes of the AMLA; e) adding unlawful activities under Sec.3(i) of the AMLA, such as violations of firearms and ammunitions regulation act, cybercrimes, violations of strategic trade management act (re: weapons of mass destruction), and tax evasion; among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2023-08-08

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT IDENTIFYING THE PHILIPPINE MARITIME FEATURES OF THE WEST PHILIPPINE SEA, DEFINING THEIR RESPECTIVE APPLICABLE BASELINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reinforce our territorial and marine rights in the West Philippine Sea, establish relevant baselines by legislation, enforce the arbitral Award, and define applicable baselines.
 
Intends to enforce the Award and ensure that the Philippines is the first claimant to legislate the individual names and baselines of the claimed features.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WEST PHILIPPINE SEA since 2023-08-08

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PENAL CODE, ARTICLE 310, TO INCREASE THE PENALTIES IN CERTAIN INSTANCES OF QUALIFIED THEFT
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend Chapter 3, Article 310 of Act No. 3815, also known as the Revised Penal Code, by increasing the penalties for some instances of qualified theft.
 
SECTION 1
 
“Art. 310. Qualified Theft”¦THE PENALTY OF RECLUSION TEMPORAL IN ITS
MAXIMUM PERIOD TO RECLUSION PERPETUA SHALL BE IMPOSED IF THE PROPERTY IS TAKEN ON THE OCCASION OF THE FOLLOWING OR IMMEDIATELY THEREAFTER:
 
”¦ANY OTHER CALAMITY NATURAL OR MAN-MADE;
 
CIVIL DISRUPTION OR DISRUPTION, PUBLIC WANT OR EMERGENCY; AND
 
ACCIDENTS INVOLVING LAND, SEA, AIR AND TRANSPORT”¦SHALL ALSO APPLY IF THE PROPERTY IS TAKEN FROM A VICTIM OF A CRIME COMMITTED BY ANOTHER, OR FROM PERSONS IN DISTRESS.
 
THE PENALTY OF RECLUSION PERPETUA SHALL BE IMPOSED IF THE OFFENDER IS A LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENT OR OFFICER; A BARANGAY OFFICIAL”¦; A FIREMAN OF
THE BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION”¦ENTRUSTED WITH A DUTY TO RENDER ASSISTANCE ON THE FOREGOING OCCURRENCES.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2023-08-08

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 386, ALSO KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, ARTICLE 1032, ON UNWORTHINESS TO SUCCEED
rows.abstract:
Seeks to include parents who induce their sons to lead corrupt or immoral lives - in the list of people who are disqualified or incapable of succeeding by reason of unworthiness.
 
Proposes to amend Article 1032 of Republic Act No. 386, also known as the Civil Code of the Philippines to read as follows:
 
SECTION 1
 
“Art. 1032 . . . incapable of succeeding by reason of unworthiness:
 
. . . Parents who have abandoned their children or induced (their daughters) THEM to lead a corrupt or immoral life, or attempted against their virtue;
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2023-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR RESTRICTIONS ON GARNISHMENT OF COMPENSATION DUE FOR PERSONAL SERVICES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to regulate the garnishment of compensation arising from employment.
 
Defines garnishment as any legal or equitable procedure through which the earnings of any individual are required to be withheld for payment of any debt.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2023-08-08

rows.author: I051;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE GRANTS TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FOR SUPERVISED VISITATION CENTERS
rows.abstract:
Aims to protect children from the trauma of witnessing or experiencing violence or abuse during parent-child visitation exchanges.   Provide safe havens for parents and children to promote continuity and stability.
 Defines family violence as any act or threatened act of violence, including any forceful detention of an individual, which - 1) results or threatens to result in physical injury, and is committed such person is or was related by blood or marriage or otherwise legally related or with whom such person is or was lawfully residing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2023-08-08

rows.author: K036;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING ANTI-AGRICULTURAL SMUGGLING MEASURES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10845, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-AGRICULTURAL SMUGGLING ACT OF 2016, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to establish a National Anti-Smuggling Council and Task Force and lengthen the detention period for those suspected of being smugglers.

Seeks to amend the title of  RA10845 to read as follows:

AN ACT DECLARING LARGE-SCALE AGRICULTURAL SMUGGLING, HOARDING, PROFITEERING, AND CARTEL AS ECONOMIC SABOTAGE . . .

Proposes to insert Section 3A after Section 3 of RA10845 to read as follows:

Section 3A. . . Hoarding, profiteering, or cartel, . . . as they involve sugar, corn, pork, poultry, garlic, onion, carrots, fish, and cruciferous vegetables, in its raw state, or which have undergone the simple processes of preparation or preservation for the market, with a minimum amount of one million pesos (P1,000,000.00), or rice, with a minimum amount of ten million pesos (Plo,000,000.00), as valued by the Bureau of Customs (BOC) for imports or by the Department of Agriculture for domestically produced commodities, shall constitute economic sabotage.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09284

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE A CIRCULAR ECONOMY
rows.abstract:
Seeks to promote and integrate within our framework the concept of circular economy.
Aims to reduce our carbon footprint and resource consumption by reusing, reducing and recycling plastics and promoting sustainable waste management in our country.

rows.author: K022;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING PANGARAP CENTERS IN ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS IN THE COUNTRY AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to create a One-Stop Shop for all state-controlled provident funds and other legally required benefit institutions in each and every legislative district of the nation to reduce the burden of complicated registration, contribution collection, loan application processing, and release of loans and pensions, among other processes.
 
Provides that each Pangarap Center shall consist of duly designated representatives from the Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Social Security System (SSS), Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) and the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2023-08-09

rows.abstract:
Seeks to shield customers from criminal groups and online thieves who prey on bank accounts, e-wallets, and other financial accounts or seduce account holders into engaging in fraudulent activity.

Intends to prohibit money mules, account takeover, phishing, and other social engineering schemes and declares the large-scale commission of such crimes as a form of economic sabotage.
